source: Minchat Shai on Gen 40:2 quoting the Ramah
claim_en: sar ha-OFIM ('the chief of the bakers'): 'this alone is full with vav AND yod; the rest of the Torah writes ha-ofim lean-vav full-yod' — exact: the one doubly-full bakers-word at the pair's introduction, the four lean stations following (40:16, 40:20, 40:22, 41:10 — asserted).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 40:10 (the Hilleli and Yerushalmi codices; the Ramah; Masoret HaMasoret)
claim_en: sarigim ('three BRANCHES'): the Hilleli wrote it doubly full, the Yerushalmi codex doubly lean — 'and I fear error, for ALL OUR BOOKS write it full-first-lean-second, like NEITHER of them' — MS with the Ramah and a handwritten Masorah against both codices. SNAPSHOT stands with the books: full-first-lean-second, once in the Torah. The Kitzur counts the lean skeleton toward 'the fathers of the world' (named).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 40:10 quoting the Ramah
claim_en: The branches-word FLIPS ITS YOD between dream and interpretation: the telling's sarigim is full-first-lean-second (40:10); the interpretation's ha-sarigim is lean-first-full-second (40:12) — the Ramah rules both, and the stream writes both, each once.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 40:19 quoting the Ramah
claim_en: The Ramah's still-word rule: 'every od and be-od in the Torah is FULL with vav except TWO lean — sign: all the days of the earth (8:22), and the men said to Lot, whom ELSE have you here (19:12).' The lemma-filtered census lands exactly on his two signs; the span's own be-od pair (40:13, 40:19) full, asserted.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 40:20 (the Masorah; the Hilleli; the Ramah; Radak's retraction)
claim_en: huledet ('Pharaoh's BIRTH-day'): Radak's Michlol ruled it full-with-vav like Ezekiel's; the Masorah, all the books, the Hilleli, and the Ramah write it LEAN — and Radak himself retracted in the Shorashim. SNAPSHOT lean, once in the Torah: the grammarian corrected by the counting tradition, on the record.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 40:1 (the Masorah's seven)
claim_en: la-adonehem ('against their LORD'): 'every lordship-word behind the prefix letters leaves the aleph SILENT — except SEVEN that sound it, and this is one.' SNAPSHOT writes the sounded aleph — the compound half-vowel under it, in-stream: the seven-list's station instrumented.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 40:1 (the Masorah)
claim_en: la-adonehem stands ONCE in the Torah; the Kitzur's pair is 'who say to their lords: bring, and let us drink' (Amos, outside the instrument) — there over drink, here over drink: the sages' fly in the cup. Census locked.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 40:6 (the Masorah)
claim_en: zoafim ('downcast') — once in the Torah; the Kitzur's partner: 'why should he see your faces DOWNCAST' (Daniel's food-refusal, outside the instrument) — there over eating, here over eating.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 40:23 (the Masorah)
claim_en: ve-lo zakhar ('and he did NOT REMEMBER') — the adjacency stands once in the Torah; the Kitzur's chain: the butler forgot Joseph, Joash forgot Jehoiada's kindness (and killed Zechariah his son), and 'He remembered not His footstool' — ingratitude counted up to the Temple's fall. The Torah-side station locked; the partners named.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 40:16 (the Sephardic books and the old print)
claim_en: ki tov patar ('that he had interpreted WELL'): MS's books rule ki 'with GALGAL (the wheel-accent), not with maqqef' — the unjoined half verified in-stream; SNAPSHOT writes the munach where the Sephardic books write the wheel: galgal-class station 7.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 40:1/7/9/22 (four accent rulings)
claim_en: The chapter's join-or-stroke set, all four matching MS: mashqe UNJOINED and melekh JOINED at 40:1 (checked); bet of 'his master's house' (40:7) and sar of 'the chief of the bakers' (40:22) each carrying the merkha-stroke, not maqqef; ve-hine (40:9) joined, not stroked (asserted).

The pointing file: u-va-gefen ('and on the vine') with the gimel dagesheed (checked); khe-forachat's kaf and ve-mishmar's bet soft (asserted); shemo (40:15) end-stressed against the lexicon's custom — 'the Masorah: none other so' (named); va-hashivkha with patach against its segol-twin (Deut 28:68), the Masorah's hooks-of-the-pillars sign (named); the books that err adding et at 40:21 corrected (named).
